terms.gloss: to be relevant, bear on the matter
terms.grammar: phrase: pertineō, pertinēre, with ad rem
evidence: Cic. Div. 2.98: sī ad rem pertinet (Lewis & Short, s.v. pertineō)
Cic. Fam. 13.13: sī quid hoc ad rem pertinet
terms.comment: The usual way; with another noun, ad hanc quaestiōnem pertinet, “it’s relevant to this question”.

evidence: Cic. Caecin. 58: nihil ad rem pertinet (Lewis & Short, s.v. pertineō)
terms.comment: Often without the verb: Nihil ad rem!, “That’s beside the point!”

terms.gloss: foreign to, out of place in, irrelevant to
terms.grammar: adjective, with ab + ablative or the dative
terms.comment: Literally “belonging to another”: what does not belong to the matter in hand.

phrases.latin: cum virtūtibus tum etiam fortūnā, sī quid hoc ad rem pertinet
phrases.english: in his virtues and also in his fortune, if this is relevant at all

phrases.latin: Nihil ad rem! Respondē ad id quod rogāvī.
phrases.english: That’s beside the point! Answer what I asked.

sources: Lewis & Short: pertineo · Lewis & Short: alienus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. relevant.
Cicero quoted as Lewis & Short quotes him.
